title: The Safehouse of Geneva
premise: Gideon Nystrom, a fixer for a deniable embassy in Geneva, discovers the safe house where 'the incident' happened has been listed for sale online, its interior photographed down to the bloodstain he never reported. The listing is bait from Ilse Brandt, the widow of the man Gideon was ordered to erase, who knows what's hidden inside: a ledger proving the embassy's director sold identities to war criminals. To survive, Gideon must decide whether to protect the institution that owns him or hand the ledger to Ilse and finally confess his role in her husband's death. In the end he burns the safe house himself, gives Ilse the ledger, and walks into an interrogation room of his own choosing — trading his secret for a night's sleep.
about_author: Lena Villalobos is a former translator for humanitarian organizations who spent six years in Geneva watching diplomacy's quiet machinery up close. She writes thrillers about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Insomniac and hollowed out, Gideon scrolls real estate listings at 3 a.m. and finds the Rue de la Cité safe house for sale — with photos showing the study where everything happened, including a detail only someone present would know. He reports it to Director Voss, who orders him to handle it quietly. Emotional beat: dread reawakened; the past knocking politely on the door.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Gideon attends the viewing posing as a buyer and finds Ilse Brandt waiting, calm and prepared, reciting details of the incident she couldn't know unless she'd read the file. She gives him 72 hours to bring her what her husband died protecting. POV shifts briefly to Ilse, revealing grief weaponized into precision. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he is also prey.

chapters.title: Housekeeping
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He sweeps the safe house, finds it already compromised — a listening device newer than the incident itself — and realizes Voss may have orchestrated the listing as loyalty test or trap. He lies to Voss about progress while quietly copying the incident file. Emotional beat: paranoia curdling into betrayal; the first crack in his obedience.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Flashback chapters braided with present action: how her husband Anton, an archivist, discovered the ledger mapping sold identities to atrocity, and why he trusted the wrong fixer with it. In the present, Ilse meets a journalist who warns her that everyone who touches the ledger dies documented. Emotional beat: love transmuted into vengeance, and doubt about whether vengeance will be enough.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He retrieves the ledger from a dead-drop inside Geneva's old customs tunnel, but finds it incomplete — one page missing, the page naming the buyer who ordered Anton silenced. Voss summons him; Gideon performs loyalty flawlessly while planning defection. Emotional beat: the vertigo of double life; competence as camouflage.

chapters.title: What the Camera Saw
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She reveals her leverage: the listing photos were taken by a hidden camera that recorded the incident — recording Gideon hesitating before following his order. She doesn't want him destroyed; she wants him to choose. Meanwhile Voss's cleaners begin closing in on both of them. Emotional beat: unexpected mercy that cuts deeper than threat.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He traces the missing page to Voss's private vault and breaks in during a diplomatic reception, discovering the buyer is a sitting minister whose protection explains the embassy's immunity. He photographs everything, then trips a silent alarm. Emotional beat: no way back; theft as self-definition.

chapters.title: Rue de la Cité
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converge at the safe house, where Ilse waits and Voss's cleaners arrive early. A tense standoff in the rooms where Anton died; Gideon shields Ilse, kills for the second time in his life, and understands the incident was never behind him — it was rehearsal. Emotional beat: climax; violence stripped of abstraction.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With cleaners dead and Voss exposed, Gideon negotiates not escape but surrender: the full ledger, the photos, and his own confession delivered to the federal prosecutor, in exchange for Ilse walking free. Voss offers him promotion instead of ruin — the old bargain, one last time. Emotional beat: refusing the only deal he was ever built to accept.

chapters.title: Sold, As Is
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, then Gideon's final pages. The safe house sells to an ordinary family; the ledger goes public; Voss is arrested in a corridor with cameras rolling. Gideon testifies, then visits the empty house one last time and sleeps — truly sleeps — in the room where it began. Emotional beat: resolution; survival's price paid, and belonging found in owning what he did.
